title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily — 17 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart, so this ordering is inferred; citation evidence is too sparse to measure popularity for same-day papers.

sections.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally teleport logical states between two distance-three surface-code qubits on a 41-physical-qubit superconducting circuit and find that repeated stabilizer measurements after merging patches restore fault tolerance and improve fidelity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report logical teleportation of Z- and X-eigenstates with success probabilities up to 0.65 and 0.73, respectively, and observe that repeated stabilizer measurements restore fault tolerance after the merge step.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; lattice-surgery operations on two distance-three surface-code logical qubits in a 41-physical-qubit superconducting circuit
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small-code demonstration, not evidence of logical-error suppression at larger code distances; the authors identify remaining hardware noise and suggest extending the method to arbitrary-state teleportation and full tomography.
sections.ranking_evidence: Strongest direct attention signal found in this batch: the paper appeared in SciRate’s daily top-paper listing and received independent coverage from Quantum Zeitgeist. The experiment reports a concrete fault-tolerant lattice-surgery operation rather than a forecast.

sections.title: Observation of temporal routing of topological edge states
sections.abstract: In a coupled nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger circuit lattice, the authors observe edge-state exchange slow with increasing excitation and eventually localize, demonstrating temporal routing in physical time.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe a progression from periodic interchain exchange to slowed exchange and then localization as excitation voltage rises, attributing the routing behavior to nonlinearity.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; temporal voltage evolution in an electrical circuit lattice of two coupled nonlinear SSH chains
sections.unique_caveat: The observed dynamics are limited to a finite time window by circuit dissipation, which constrains how long the routing can be followed.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed across nonlinear physics, condensed matter, and optics; the arXiv comment says it is to be published in Physical Letters A, and a publisher record is available. It directly reports temporal dynamics rather than a spatial-to-time analogy.

sections.title: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
sections.abstract: XRISM/Resolve spectra spatially resolve chromium and manganese emission in Tycho’s Type Ia supernova remnant, constraining its ejecta and progenitor models while leaving multiple explosion scenarios viable.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find Cr and Mn lines strongest in the Fe-bright northeast and northwest regions; measured mass ratios are compatible with more than one one-dimensional explosion model, though the best-fitting models imply progenitor metallicities they judge too high for Tycho’s location.
sections.evidence_type: observational; spatially resolved X-ray spectroscopy of Tycho’s supernova remnant with XRISM/Resolve, interpreted using plasma and explosion models
sections.unique_caveat: The northern and southern regions have limited exposure: chromium there is only marginal at 90% confidence, and low counts do not support firm conclusions; model choices also leave the progenitor scenario ambiguous.
sections.ranking_evidence: The arXiv comment reports acceptance in Astronomy & Astrophysics. The result uses XRISM/Resolve’s high spectral resolution to constrain elemental abundances and spatial distributions in a specific remnant.

sections.title: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
sections.abstract: The authors release a near-infrared JWST photometric and astrometric catalog of Omega Centauri containing about 677,000 sources, including more than 86,000 below HST’s detection limit.
sections.claimed_result: From NIRCam and NIRISS observations, the authors report over 90% recovery of overlapping HST sources, 86,000-plus sources fainter than HST’s detection limit, and single-image astrometric precision near 150 microarcseconds for bright sources.
sections.evidence_type: observational; custom reduction of JWST NIRCam and NIRISS imaging from three programs, cross-matched to HST catalog data
sections.unique_caveat: Precision and completeness vary with brightness and field location; the paper reports localized edge deviations reaching about 4 mas, so the best quoted precision should not be assumed across the full catalog.
sections.ranking_evidence: A substantial JWST data release with stated source counts, completeness, and astrometric precision; cross-listed in Galactic astronomy and stellar astrophysics and marked as submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics.

sections.title: Atomic-scale Imaging of Time Reversal Breaking Supercurrents in Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈
sections.abstract: Using spectroscopic imaging and a dual artificial neural network, the authors infer repeatable supercurrent-loop networks in a cuprate superconductor across hole densities 0.17–0.22.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use a dual-ANN VMAP to map energy-resolved electronic density-of-states images to current speeds and report loop networks with inferred speeds of 1,250–4,000 m/s, consistent with cited disordered d-wave predictions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; spectroscopic-imaging scanning tunneling microscopy on Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈, analyzed with the authors’ dual-ANN mapping method
sections.unique_caveat: The currents are inferred from spectroscopic maps through a model-based ANN mapping, rather than directly measured as current; independent validation with a complementary probe remains important.
sections.ranking_evidence: Included for a specific, potentially significant experimental claim—repeatable current-loop patterns, junctions satisfying Kirchhoff’s law, and inferred speeds—not for demonstrated broad attention. No independent expert validation or cross-subfield listing was found in the sources checked.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Operations and temporal control in physical hardware: lattice-surgery logical transfer and nonlinearity-controlled edge-state routing are distinct experiments and not mutual confirmation.

Instrument-led astrophysics and reusable data: XRISM/Resolve observations in Tycho and JWST NIRCam/NIRISS catalog work on Omega Centauri use different instruments and targets but turn improved spatial or spectral information into model constraints.

Model-assisted extraction of difficult signals: the cuprate paper maps STM spectra to a current field with a dual ANN, while the XRISM analysis compares measured line ratios with explosion models; the inferences are distinct and model-dependent.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: The logical-operation experiment tests distance-three qubits; synthesis: repeat at larger code distances and test whether fidelity gains persist as depth and device size increase.
Topological routing is limited by circuit dissipation; synthesis: lower circuit losses and vary excitation to test how long exchange/localization regimes remain observable.

Tycho’s Cr/Mn constraints are exposure-limited in some regions and compatible with multiple one-dimensional models; synthesis: obtain deeper spatially resolved spectra and compare with three-dimensional models.
Cuprate current fields are inferred through an ANN mapping; synthesis: test held-out spectra, additional samples/dopings, and an independent current-sensitive measurement.
The Omega Centauri catalog is intended to support future monitoring; synthesis: combine new JWST epochs with the long HST baseline to test central-star motions and field-dependent systematics.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest attention signal is a superconducting-circuit demonstration of logical-qubit teleportation; alongside it, a circuit-lattice experiment and two major astrophysical datasets show how better control and instruments expose dynamics hidden to coarser methods. The cuprate current-loop report is potentially consequential but remains method-dependent and unconfirmed by an independent probe.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.text: Daily window 2026-11-17 through 2026-11-17; batch date 2026-11-17; snapshot 2026-11-18T17:32:00Z. Queried all 11 configured arXiv archives in combined submitted-date and last-updated-date requests. The new-submission query returned 328 records and 328 unique arXiv IDs; no older-paper revisions surfaced in the matching update-date query. Per-archive appearance counts include cross-lists. No numeric trend score was assigned; inference favors coverage/publication status, concrete results, cross-listing, and data or method contributions. Semantic Scholar Graph current citation and influential-citation totals were zero for the five selected papers, not period gains.
